Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.query

Class QueryFactory

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.QueryFactory
public final class QueryFactory extends Object
Starts queries on one connection, with the grammar and processor of its database. 

 QueryFactory db = SQLiteQuery.of(connection);
 List<Map<String, Object>> rows = db.table("users").where("active", true).get();

The core Connection cannot start a query itself, because it never knows which database module's grammar to use; the database module's shortcut, or of(org.aristonis.diwan.database.Connection, org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.QueryGrammar, org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.Processor), ties the three together instead.

Instances are immutable and safe to share between threads; the builders they return are not.

    • truncate

      public void truncate(List<String> tables, boolean cascade)
      Empties several tables in one call. When the grammar needs several statements, they run in one transaction, unless the connection is already inside one.

      PostgreSQL runs one truncate that restarts identities. SQLite defers foreign-key checks to the commit, so the order is irrelevant, but a table outside the list that still refers to an emptied one makes the commit fail and undoes everything, unless cascade is set: SQLite then empties the referring tables too, as PostgreSQL does.

      Parameters:
      tables - the table names, never null, none null or blank, optionally schema.table; empty runs nothing
      cascade - whether tables that refer to these are emptied too, where the database can
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if tables is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if a name is null or blank
      UnsupportedOperationException - if cascade is true and the grammar cannot
      QueryException - if the database refuses a statement; inside the transaction, every statement is then undone

    • on

      public QueryFactory on(Connection other)
      Returns a factory with the same grammar and processor that runs on another connection of the same database, such as the connection a transaction callback receives.

      Code inside connection.transaction(tx -> ...) must run on tx; this lets it keep using the factory it already has without naming the database's module.

      Parameters:
      other - the connection to run on, never null
      Returns:
      a factory bound to other, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if other is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if other talks to a different kind of database or uses a different table prefix
